title: Fate and Ragnarök
subtitle: An ending built into the world

learningObjectives.text: Describe the renewed world in Völuspá 59 and Gylfaginning 58.
Distinguish the poem from Snorri's prose retelling.

prose.author: Snorri Sturluson
prose.locator: Gylfaginning 58, the renewed world; local text normalized characters 159549-159741
prose.excerpt: 58. Then said Ganglere: Do any gods live then? Is there any earth or heaven? Har answered: The earth rises again from the sea, and is green and fair. The fields unsown produce their harvests.
prose.note: Verbatim Rasmus B. Anderson translation excerpt; whitespace normalized.

poem.author: Anonymous Old Norse poets
poem.locator: Völuspá, stanzas 59-61; local text normalized characters 45061-45558
poem.excerpt: 59. Now do I see | the earth anew Rise all green | from the waves again; The cataracts fall, | and the eagle flies, And fish he catches | beneath the cliffs. 60. The gods in Ithavoll | meet together, Of the terrible girdler | of earth they talk, And the mighty past | they call to mind, And the ancient runes | of the Ruler of Gods. 61. In wondrous beauty | once again Shall the golden tables | stand mid the grass, Which the gods had owned | in the days of old, . . . . . . . . | . . . . . . . .
poem.note: Verbatim Henry Adams Bellows translation excerpt; whitespace normalized.

narrativeBlocks.title: The story continues after catastrophe
narrativeBlocks.body: Völuspá does not end its vision with the burning and sinking of the old world. Stanza 59 describes the earth rising green again from the waves.

narrativeBlocks.title: Snorri's prose question and answer
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translated; whitespace normalized): “58. Then said Ganglere: Do any gods live then? Is there any earth or heaven? Har answered: The earth rises again from the sea, and is green and fair. The fields unsown produce their harvests.”

narrativeBlocks.title: Compare poem and retelling
narrativeBlocks.body: Völuspá speaks through a prophetic voice; Gylfaginning retells the events in a question-and-answer frame. Keep each work's wording and framing attached to the claim.

narrativeBlocks.title: An ending with a sequel
narrativeBlocks.body: Both excerpts make renewal part of their account, but their narrative forms differ. Do not turn these two texts into a single timeless Norse canon.

quiz.prompt: What does Völuspá 59 say happens to the earth?

choices.text: It remains sunk beneath the sea
It is replaced by an untouched world with no prior catastrophe
It rises green again from the waves

quiz.explanation: The stanza names renewal after the preceding catastrophe.
